elements.texte:
[cheerful] A transaction ends with COMMIT or with ROLLBACK.

Your turn!

COMMIT commits all the changes in the transaction.

ROLLBACK rolls back all the ones not committed yet.

After COMMIT, you can no longer use ROLLBACK to roll back this transaction.

These guarantees have a name: ACID.

Atomicity: all or nothing, as with COMMIT and ROLLBACK.

Consistency: the database’s rules are always followed.

Isolation: transactions don’t get mixed up.

Durability: a committed change stays recorded.

In the next lesson, you’ll learn to roll back part of a transaction with SAVEPOINT.
